a.c: To travel the continent and map every last corner.

Trekkers once put up all kinds of signposts on their own to help travelers navigate the Wilds. Time and weather have since worn many of these markers beyond recognition. The Trekker Association stepped in to keep them standing, and Leafia handles the repairs in the most treacherous terrain. No one knows those remote, unforgiving lands better than she does.

Nova Geography Journal: Spotlight on the Gale Owl
Guest Writer: Leafia
... When nesting, Gale Owls love lining their nests with stiff paper. They will even swoop down and snatch letters right out of a Courier Trekker's hands mid-delivery...
... They don't go "Hoooo, hoot-hoot, hoot-hoot!" like normal owls. Field observations show that adult Gale Owls actually let out a "hoo—hoo—gaaahhh!" when calling for a mate...

"It's almost time."
Lulled by the midday sun, the young girl was drifting off to sleep. Even half-awake, she kept a tight grip on the hair of the young woman carrying her to keep from slipping off those slender shoulders.
"Ow, ow, ow! Easy on the hair, Leafia." The young woman pried her locks free from the child's fingers and looped her arms securely around her legs, steadying her wobbly passenger.
Waiting in silence had to be pure torture for a kid who couldn't sit still for long. Realizing this, the young woman struck up a conversation. "Do you know why I brought you here?"
Leafia sighed. "Getting forgetful, Horizon? You already told me we're here to see the well with no shadow."
"R-Right, of course! Good memory!" Covering her slip-up, Horizon tried to hook the girl's interest with the legend behind it. "They say on certain days, this well swallows up every shadow, leaving no darkness beneath the sun."
"Wow..." Leafia deadpanned, humoring her. "Could today be that special day? How exciting."
"You bet! You don't get to see a sight like this every day." Better yet, it was free. She didn't have to beg the Trekker Association for ticket money, making it the ultimate spot for babysitting, Horizon added to herself.
Leafia kept her eyes glued to the edge of the well. As sunlight poured straight down, it silently claimed every bit of ground, devouring the shadows inch by inch.
At that moment, the sun hung directly above the world.
"Pretty amazing, right?" Horizon carried Leafia all the way around the well, and sure enough, there wasn't a trace of a shadow anywhere. "As for how it works... Want to join our Trekker Association? The scholar ladies there can explain it all to you."
"Hmm..."
Horizon flicked Leafia's forehead. "Just kidding! Come on, don't make that face. Our Association is great! We have tons of cool stuff you've never seen before."
"Do you have those drawings you showed me last time? The ones covered in lines ... called 'maps'?"
"Oh? You still remember those?"
Of course. Why else would I have come out with you? Leafia looked at Horizon and swallowed the thought, too shy to say it out loud.
Here Horizon had been racking her brains for a fun trip to broaden the kid's horizons, when she could have just stayed indoors. The everyday items lying around the Association were more than enough to leave the girl spellbound.
This kid was so easy to please, Horizon marveled. "Let's head back to the Trekkers' House. I'll dig out the maps for every single region and show them to you."
"Okay! Then... While we're at it, I guess I'll listen to why this well doesn't have a shadow."
"... Could you at least pretend to be a little curious?"
"Uh, wow... I'm dying to know... Urgh, cough, cough... Horizon, slow down!"
"Hmph, I shouldn't have even asked. Close your mouth and hold onto my neck! And stop pulling my hair!"

With Leafia still clutching her hair, a disheveled Horizon banged open the doors of the Trekkers' House.
"Somebody help me pry this kid off!" Spotting her partner Kinsa trying to sneak away, Horizon grabbed her arm. She knew Kinsa hated babysitting, but a deal was a deal, and they'd promised to help each other out. "Either take her, or go dig out all the maps in the Trekkers' House for me."
"I'll get the maps." Backing away fast, Kinsa didn't hesitate for a second. She bolted back to the office, loudly declaring she would gather every last map they had, old and new, from north to south.
Hearing that the lady was going to get the drawings, Leafia climbed right down from Horizon's shoulders and looked up, her eyes hinting: I want to go look for them with her, too.
Horizon was helpless against those big, pleading eyes. "Wait up, Kinsa! We're coming with you!"
Kinsa couldn't escape babysitting duty after all, though she soon breathed a sigh of relief. The young girl Horizon had brought along sat quietly amidst the piles of parchment, poring over the maps as if holding the most precious treasures in the world.
Kinsa shot Horizon a look that clearly asked: Where on earth did you find and trick such an angel into following you?
Well... Horizon thought back to a month ago, when a missing persons commission had taken her deep into the backcountry where they first met.
Fresh off a Monolith expedition, Horizon had heard of a nearby town famous for its sweetbrew. As the Association's self-proclaimed number one connoisseur of the drink, she had planned to spend her commission reward on a nice treat, only to arrive at the town gates and find the place in an uproar.
"E-Excuse me, are you with the Trekker Association? Several of our kids have gone missing!" Spotting Horizon's uniform, a frantic woman clung to her sleeve like a lifeline. "We'll pay whatever it costs, just please help us find them!"
With a verbal promise of a barrel of sweetbrew as payment, the Trekker set off to find the kids.
Expecting vicious kidnappers, Horizon braced herself for a tough fight. Yet before she even got far into the wilderness, the very kids from the missing posters strolled out of the hills, chatting and laughing.
"W-We're the Treasure Squad! We went looking for treasure."
"We weren't worried about getting lost. Leafia knows her way around, so we just had to follow her to get back home."
Horizon looked at the girl leading the pack. Small, thin, and dead silent, she looked a few years younger than the rest.
"You've got quite the nerve." With a sigh, Horizon herded the kids back to town like a flock of sheep, none of them having a clue about the scolding waiting for them at home.
She held off on collecting her reward, too. The sweetbrew shop owner's son was one of the runaways, and she figured her drink wouldn't taste very good with a wailing kid in the background anyway.
The Treasure Squad quickly disbanded as each child was dragged home, leaving only Leafia, the fearless navigator, standing beside Horizon.
"Why aren't you going home to your mom and dad?"
Leafia shook her head. Horizon immediately understood what that meant.
Not knowing how to comfort a child, Horizon racked her brains to change the subject. "So why were those kids following you back there?"
Leafia sighed. "You're a little forgetful, Miss Trekker. Like they said, I know the way."
"See? The way home is right here on this picture."
Surprised, Horizon looked at the tattered old map in Leafia's hands. Faint pencil marks showed where revisions had been made.
"What are these marks?"
"I fixed it based on the roads I've walked. There aren't any bigger maps in town."
Now that caught Horizon's interest. She bent down, beaming at the child.
"Hey, kiddo, want to come with me? Where I'm from, we have tons of bigger and better maps."
"Okay."

Several years had passed since Horizon brought Leafia back to the Trekker Association.
Leafia was now known as the Association's number one surveyor. Of course, unlike a certain self-proclaimed sweetbrew connoisseur, Leafia had actually earned her title in the eyes of every single member.
"Ahem! I think the time has come!" Horizon led Leafia into the headquarters' warehouse and began digging through crates of documents, models, and spare parts. None of them seemed to be what she was looking for.
Reaching into the stack of crates on the far left, Leafia pulled out a round magical instrument. "Looking for this, President Horizon?"
"Yes, that's it! Wait, how did you know where it was?"
"Mikan and I needed files from here for the Journal, so we beat you to it and went through the whole warehouse ages ago." Leafia fiddled with the dusty instrument. Thick mist clouded the crystal dome on top, hiding whatever lay inside.
"We didn't know what it was, though. The records Mikan found just said it belonged to the best surveyor from the old expedition team."
"And you already guessed I brought you here for it?"
"Yeah. Because I'm the best surveyor in the Association now."
Horizon pinched Leafia's cheek. The girl had stated it as a simple matter of fact, and Horizon just couldn't help herself.
"Let's see if you can wake it up with your magic first."
Leafia channeled her magic along the instrument's engravings. Instantly, light flared inside the crystal dome, clearing the mist. Instead of the flashy magic circle she had pictured, the dome held a simple, unadorned compass.
"Those records you and Mikan found were spot on. This relic from the Great Expedition Era is called the True North. As for how to use it... Beats me, haha."
Tuning out the President's unhelpful remark, Leafia studied the instrument closely, cradling it just like she used to hold her favorite treasures as a child.
"Not too plain for you, is it?"
"Of course not. Surveying isn't about being flashy. It's about getting the truest data."

d.m: You learned a valuable lesson in wilderness survival, even if your instructor's methods were ... a bit questionable.
